Discrete

/dih-SKREET/ · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Discrete means individually separate and distinct — made of clearly divided parts rather than one continuous whole

Discrete means individually separate and distinct — made of clearly divided parts rather than one continuous whole. The bridge project was planned as four discrete stages, each with its own budget, crew, and deadline.

Worked Example

The questionnaire sorts ages into discrete categories — under 18, 18 to 34, 35 to 64, and 65 and up — with no overlap between them.

The age brackets are separate, non-overlapping units with clean boundaries between them. That clear division into distinct parts is exactly what discrete captures.

How Discrete Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

separate

separate: kept apart; not joined

distinct

distinct: clearly different and individual

self-contained

self-contained: complete in itself; independent of the rest

Antonyms

continuous

continuous: unbroken; without divisions

merged

merged: combined into one

How Strong Is It? — separate → isolated → discrete

separate vs. discrete

separate vs. discrete: Separate is the milder, everyday word: two separate rooms can still share a door.

isolated vs. discrete

isolated vs. discrete: Isolated is stronger than discrete: an isolated outpost is not just a distinct unit — it is cut off from everything around it, which discrete never implies.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart

Root — cret

Root — cret: sifted, separated (Latin cernere, cretus — to sift, to distinguish)

Put it together

Put it together: From Latin discretus, "sifted apart": dis- (apart) + cretus (sifted, separated) — like grain sifted into clearly separate piles, each part distinct from the rest.

Use the root in a new word: discerning

Use the root in a new word: discerning: A discerning editor can sift one promising manuscript from a pile of ordinary ones.

Root Check

Word Choice

Academic / technical

Spelling is everything here: discrete (-crete) means separate and distinct — discrete steps, discrete categories, discrete units. Discreet (-eet) is a different word entirely in modern English: it means careful and tactful about what you reveal. Data comes in discrete units; a friend who keeps your news quiet is being discreet. Quick test: if you can swap in "separate," the word you want is discrete.
